paper.title: Mindfulness training reduces exam anxiety in undergraduates

paper_text:
Mindfulness training reduces exam anxiety in undergraduates
Smith, J., Lee, K., Tan, M.  J. Fake Psychology, 2020

Abstract
We randomised 120 undergraduates to eight weeks of mindfulness training or a waitlist control. Training reduced self-reported exam anxiety relative to control.

Results
Table 2 reports the anxiety scores. Mindfulness training produced a large reduction in exam anxiety (d = 1.8, 95% CI 1.4 to 2.2).

Discussion
The effect was large and was not explained by age or course. The sample came from a single university.

alerts.description: A correction notice was published for this paper.

notice.text:
Correction to: Mindfulness training reduces exam anxiety in undergraduates

In the original article, the effect size in Table 2 was reported incorrectly because of a calculation error. The correct value is d = 0.8 (95% CI 0.5 to 1.1), not d = 1.8. The direction of the effect and the conclusion that training reduced anxiety are unchanged. The authors apologise for the error.

draft_text:
Brief mindfulness programmes for exam stress

1. Introduction
Exam anxiety harms performance and wellbeing. Smith et al. [12] found a large effect (d = 1.8), so we expect mindfulness to strongly reduce anxiety. We test a four-week version of the programme.

2. Methods
We recruited 80 students and measured anxiety with a standard questionnaire before and after the programme.

References
[12] Smith, J., Lee, K., Tan, M. (2020). Mindfulness training reduces exam anxiety in undergraduates. J. Fake Psychology.
